conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.4 and lean slightly positive: the guidance was reaffirmed about 2.5 weeks before the quarter closed, FY27 consensus sits below the guide, and the primes converted munitions contracts to multiyear deals. Against that, the 25-delta skew is +36 vol points toward puts, the name has sold beats twice in 2026 (Feb -22%, Aug -3.6% then -26% over the following weeks), and the Nov 3 Democratic sweep put the FY27 budget in doubt. So p_up is 52 on an abs move of 10.5, giving +0.42; the scaled number is much smaller than the sum because the sign is close to a coin flip, not because the move is small.
bar: Q1 FY27 revenue about $244-245M: Earnings Whispers $244.2M / EPS $0.28, whisper $0.31 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/MRCY/22753, 2026-11-03); Investing.com $245.01M / EPS $0.30 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/mercury-systems-earnings-on-deck-can-backlog-fuel-rebound-93CH-5016053, 2026-11-10). The two sources agree, and both sit inside the company's own Q1 guide: high-single-digit growth on Q1 FY26's $225.2M, adj. EBITDA margin in line with Q1 FY26's 15.8% (Q4 FY26 call, 2026-08-18). FY27 bar: company says 'approaching $1.1B' revenue and 'approaching $200M' adj. EBITDA; consensus is about $1.06B (Earnings Whispers) and Oppenheimer has $1.08B / $199M (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-mercury-systems-nasdaq-mrcy-coverage-initiated-by-analysts-at-oppenheimer-2026-10-22/).
positioning_check: Short interest 5.56M shares, 8.4 days to cover (shortsqueeze.com, page read 2026-11-10, figure about late October). FINRA-based 5.01M / 7.4 DTC at 2026-09-30 (massive.com, via search). That is roughly 9% of a ~59M share float: elevated but not extreme, and it rose into the print. Options (sealed baseline): event-implied move 9.88%; 25-delta skew +36.4 vol points, so downside protection is paid heavily; put/call open interest 0.41; ATM spread 30% of mid, so the chain is thin. Tape: down about 26% from the Aug 18 print to $77.37 on Nov 3 (Earnings Whispers), then +6.1% over 5 days and +11.1% over 20 days to $85.21 at the seal; 32% below the 52-week high. Sentiment moved from 26% bullish to neutral (Earnings Whispers). Insiders: the CEO's August sale was a tax-withholding sale; the Oct 28-30 Form 4s are annual-meeting director grants (the JANA/Ostfeld DSU grant was checked).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-16, about 2.5 weeks before fiscal Q1 closed on ~Oct 2, Mercury's 8-K (the release on the CEO contract extension to 2030) 'reaffirmed the financial guidance provided on its August 18, 2026 earnings call', and the lead director cited 'enhanced multi-year visibility and an improving organic growth outlook'. With about 85% of the quarter booked, the company was willing to restate a Q1 guide of high-single-digit growth (about $243-247M on Q1 FY26's $225.2M, a base that itself held ~$20M pulled forward from Q2) with EBITDA margin in line. The $244-245M consensus is inside that range, so a revenue miss is less likely than the 36-point put skew implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mercury has beaten revenue and been sold: Aug 2026, revenue 9% above consensus, adj. EPS $0.37 against $0.38-0.39, stock -3.57% on the day and about -26% by Nov 3. Feb 2026, a beat helped by a $30M pull-forward, -22.32%. May 2026 +10.49%; Nov 2025 +3.28% on a print that included a $20M pull-in.
findings.why_not_priced: It ran as a CEO-contract headline, not as an earnings item, and no preview we found mentions it. If the market had priced a firmed Q1, the 25-delta put skew would not be +36 vol points with a 9.9% event move; previews would quote a mid-September reaffirmation rather than 'must prove backlog can convert'.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 base and its $20M pull-in come from the Nov 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1049521/000104952125000060/a2026q1earningsreleaseex.htm). Nothing independent confirms Q1 FY27 revenue.

findings.finding: FY27 street revenue is about $1.06B (Earnings Whispers, Nov 3), and Oppenheimer's Oct 22 initiation models $1.08B and $199M EBITDA, while management guided 'approaching $1.1B' and 'approaching $200M' and reaffirmed both on Sep 16. Holding the guide on Nov 10 lifts estimates about 2-4% on revenue. Investing.com (Nov 10) says EPS estimates edged lower over 60 days, so the street is still doubting the company's number going into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When FY27/FY28 were first guided and long-term targets raised in Aug 2026, the stock fell 3.57% on the day and then about 26%. The market sold the guide because of the 35% FCF conversion and margin, not the revenue line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits below the company's own guide. If the market believed the guide, consensus would be at $1.09-1.10B, and the stock would not be 7% below the Oppenheimer $90 target that itself sits under every other target ($110 average).

findings.finding: Inside Mercury's fiscal Q1 (Jul-Sep 2026) the primes converted munitions framework agreements into very large multiyear contracts. RTX: Raytheon book-to-bill 6.54 on $52.3B, including about $23B Tomahawk, more than $14B AMRAAM, and SM-6/SM-3 multiyears. Lockheed: a $52.5B PAC-3 MSE multiyear, MFC backlog $142.5B. L3Harris: Missile Solutions book-to-bill 11.8x. Mercury said on Aug 18 that it expected 'clarity on multiyear munitions and framework tailwinds in Q1 or Q2 FY27', and those tailwinds (effectors, munitions, missile defense) are explicitly excluded from its FY27 guide. That sets up bookings or guide-color upside. Mercury's specific content on these missiles is not confirmed in any source, and subcontract flowdown usually lags the prime award by quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings surprises have been bought: Aug 2025 +26.95% on record bookings and backlog; Feb 2025 +18.51%. In Aug 2026 a record 2.28 book-to-bill did not stop a -3.57% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews expect book-to-bill to 'almost certainly fall' from 2.28 (Earnings Whispers) and do not connect the primes' Q3 multiyear conversions to Mercury's own excluded-tailwind language. If they had, previews would carry a bookings upside case and the skew would not be put-heavy.
findings.independence: Lockheed PAC-3 multiyear: https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2026-10-22-Lockheed-Martin-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results (2026-10-22). L3Harris Missile Solutions 11.8x: https://www.l3harris.com/newsroom/press-release/2026/10/l3harris-delivers-record-backlog-and-strong-third-quarter-results (2026-10-29). Mercury's own 'clarity in Q1 or Q2' wording: https://www.webull.com/news/15465970489967616 (Q4 call 2026-08-18). This is a proxy: Mercury has not confirmed content on these programs.

findings.finding: The Nov 3 midterms produced a Democratic sweep. Jefferies expects the FY27 defense budget nearer the House's $1.15T than the $1.5T request; TD Cowen said 'Trump branded programs are dead', naming Golden Dome; and LMT, LHX, RTX and NOC closed lower on Nov 4. Mercury's excluded upside list includes missile defense and space, so management will be asked about Golden Dome exposure and could temper the tailwind talk. The base FY27 guide does not depend on these programs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Mercury print fell on a budget-politics shift; the closest is the 2025 CR/shutdown period, when the stock rose 3.28% on the Nov 2025 print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sector sold off Nov 4-5. MRCY nonetheless rose 6.1% over the last 5 sessions to $85.21, so its own price has not marked down the budget risk. Mercury will be the first defense-electronics call after the election to field the question.
findings.independence: Investing.com (2026-11-10) notes defense names under pressure on budget uncertainty: https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/mercury-systems-earnings-on-deck-can-backlog-fuel-rebound-93CH-5016053. This is macro-to-company transmission that Mercury has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Curtiss-Wright, the closest listed peer in rugged embedded computing, said on its Nov 5 call that rising memory prices had put 'some pressure' on it, and that it was responding with advance buys, DPAS ratings and second sourcing. Its Defense Electronics margin fell 220bp to 27.0% on mix and R&D. Mercury relies on memory (its Q4 included 'bookings related to securing memory to support future production'), guided an unusually large Q1 cash outflow for material receipts, and saw Q4 EBITDA margin drop to 16.7% from 18.8% on contract-estimate effects. On fixed-price backlog, memory inflation is an EAC/margin risk to the 'in line with Q1 FY26' (15.8%) margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin quality has driven the bad reactions: Aug 2026, margin down 210bp YoY with revenue beating, -3.57% then -26%; Feb 2026 -22.32% when the beat was flattered by a pull-forward.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews list FCF and the contract-manufacturer transition as watch items but none names memory cost inflation for Mercury. If it were priced, previews would flag an EAC or gross-margin risk from memory, and the EPS bar would not still be $0.28-0.30 with a $0.31 whisper.
findings.independence: Industry series: DigiKey's 2026 memory shortage and price-hike note (https://www.digikey.ca/en/blog/the-2026-memory-challenge). Mercury memory bookings: Q4 call transcript https://www.webull.com/news/15465970489967616. This is a peer proxy: Mercury has not quantified any memory cost effect. It shares the CW call document with the next finding.

findings.finding: Curtiss-Wright Defense Electronics (Nov 5, 2026) grew sales only 2% (helped by a pull-in from Q4) but orders rose 27% YoY after a record Q2, on fighter, helicopter and CCA programs. Management expects 'strong sequential growth' into Q4, said the current CR (to Dec 11) is not hurting bookings, and the company raised its full-year sales outlook to 8-10%. Demand for the closest peer's rugged embedded computing was strong in the calendar quarter that overlaps Mercury's fiscal Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to peer read-throughs; Mercury's revenue beats have been sold in 2026 (see the first finding).
findings.why_not_priced: It reported five days before Mercury and is a peer, not a customer. Mercury previews (Nov 3 and Nov 10) predate it or do not cite it.
findings.independence: The call detail is from the same CW Q3 call as the memory finding (https://www.webull.com/news/15873322772030464), so the two share one document and pull in opposite directions; Kratos also raised guidance on Nov 5 (https://finviz.com/news/417590/kratos-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: about 5.56M shares short (8.4 days to cover, roughly 9% of float), up from 5.01M / 7.4 DTC at Sep 30. The stock fell about 26% between prints and sentiment reset to neutral, then rallied 11% in 20 sessions and 6% in 5 into the event. Put skew is +36 vol points but put/call open interest is only 0.41. On a clean print, a growing short with 8 days of cover is a squeeze mechanism; the rally into the print also raises the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After big drawdowns into prints the stock has ripped: May 2026 +10.49% after a 25% fall post-February; Aug 2025 +26.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew prices downside, not a squeeze. If the short base had been covered into the run-up, days to cover would have fallen from September rather than risen from 7.4 to 8.4.
findings.independence: Sep 30 FINRA-based figure via massive.com (https://massive.com/quote/mrcy). Sentiment reset and $77.37 on Nov 3: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/MRCY/22753.

findings.finding: Management guided Q1 FY27 to a 'larger than normal' cash outflow for material receipts, and FY27 FCF conversion to about 35% against a 50% target. The Q1 FCF print will be negative by design. That is a known, guided line, and the market punished the FCF guide in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 FCF-conversion guide (35%) was the main cited cause of the -3.57% day and the follow-through (Motley Fool, 2026-08-19).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it is guided and every preview names it. The residual is the size of the outflow, which is unquantified; a figure far outside 'larger than normal' would move the stock.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview repeats it: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/MRCY/22753. Same Q4 call document as the first two findings' guidance terms.

outside_window.finding: The current CR funds the government to Dec 11, 2026. A shutdown or full-year CR after that date would hit new-start awards, but it resolves after the exit window.

baseline_tension: What I found leans mildly positive and cuts against the +36.4-point put skew, but agrees with the +11% 20-day run-up. The skew most likely reflects hedging after a 26% drawdown and a name that sold its last two beats, which is why p_up sits only 2 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold beats in Feb and Aug 2026): reaffirmed-guidance finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; the consensus-below-guide finding from +1.0 to +0.7; p_up from 53 to 52
Lesson 5 (a proxy is smaller): the munitions flow-down finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, because Mercury's content on those missiles is unconfirmed

Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives; respect the skew): the budget-politics negative cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and the memory-cost negative from -0.7 to -0.5, given 8.4 days to cover. The positive lean is kept but small, with the reason given in baseline_tension
Lesson 6 (bar verified from two agreeing sources plus the company guide; window): no cap needed; the CR deadline is in outside_window
Left standing: the CW peer-orders, positioning and Q1 cash-outflow findings are unchanged
